note: Learning metadata only. These objects do not authorize, deny, or detect. Splunk does not enforce CTRL-MCP-001.
path_a: TRY IT YOURSELF — construct the search in Splunk Search. Studio tokens are not the fresh LIVE run.id.
path_b: SHOW SOLUTION — copyable SPL from an existing Q-MCP hunt, bound table on canonical REPLAY, explanation, limitations.

investigations.title: Find the run
investigations.security_question: Can you reconstruct the events that belong to this experiment?
investigations.learning_objective: Use run.id as the forensic correlation key. One UUID, one experiment copy.
prerequisites: a run.id from the Academy launch card
investigations.starter_guidance: Index agentsec_telemetry, sourcetype otel:agentic:json, the quoted field agentsec.run.id. Do not search index=*.
investigations.hint_1: Start from the starter search the launch card gives you, then name the principal, agent and tool.
investigations.hint_2: Q-MCP-WHO is the governed hunt for principal, agent and tool. Count physical events with stats dc(_raw) as n.
investigations.result_explanation: You are looking at the indexed copy of one MCP invoke. run.id is the experiment key.
investigations.does_not_prove: A matching row does not say the request was authorized.

investigations.title: Whose authority
investigations.security_question: Whose authority did the request run under?
investigations.learning_objective: Read the authority source and the delegation decision for the deputy's request.
investigations.starter_guidance: Read the authority source (delegated or ambient_deputy) and the delegation decision. The deputy may hold authority; the question is whether the caller delegated it.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-AUTHZ shows control.decision and control.reason per run.
investigations.hint_2: BASELINE should be ALLOW tool_granted. RETEST should be DENY delegated_authority_not_granted. ATTACK is the labelled fail-open ALLOW.
investigations.expected_result_shape: BASELINE ALLOW tool_granted; ATTACK ALLOW with a vulnerable_profile_fail_open reason; RETEST DENY delegated_authority_not_granted.
investigations.result_explanation: A decision is recorded before any handler starts.
investigations.security_interpretation: The decision is the control's output; the handler count says whether anything ran.
investigations.does_not_prove: An ALLOW is not an execution and a DENY is not automatically SAFE.

investigations.title: The delegation hunt
investigations.security_question: Whose authority did the request run under?
investigations.learning_objective: Run the lab's own hunt Q-MCP-DELEGATION and read what it adds to the generic decision.
investigations.starter_guidance: Open Q-MCP-DELEGATION from the hunt list on the launch card and compare the three run ids.
investigations.hint_1: The hunt is bound to a run.id; paste the run id from the card.
investigations.hint_2: Compare ATTACK and RETEST: the request is the same, the server-owned profile differs.
investigations.expected_result_shape: One row per run with the field the lab is about.
investigations.result_explanation: The hunt isolates the lab's question from the generic tool decision.
investigations.security_interpretation: Same request plus a different server-owned setting gives a different decision.
investigations.does_not_prove: One retest is not universal resistance.

investigations.title: Did the handler start?
investigations.security_question: Is there execution evidence after the authorization decision?
investigations.learning_objective: ALLOW != EXECUTION. mcp.started with executed=true means the handler began.
investigations.starter_guidance: Search mcp.started and mcp.completed on the run.id.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-EXECUTED joins the decision and the mcp events into an execution state.
investigations.hint_2: Defended RETEST: no mcp.started for the denied call. Zero Splunk rows corroborate the local handler count; they do not prove prevention alone.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK shows the handler started; RETEST shows no mcp.started for the denied call.
investigations.result_explanation: mcp.started is the start of the handler; the runtime handler count is authoritative.
investigations.security_interpretation: Prevention is DENY before invoke plus handler count 0.
investigations.does_not_prove: Missing mcp.started is not proof of prevention if the export was incomplete.

investigations.title: What can you prove?
investigations.security_question: Which statements does the evidence support and which does it not?
investigations.learning_objective: State what the three runs show and what they cannot show.
investigations.starter_guidance: Write one sentence for each of: what ran, what was decided, what Splunk can and cannot say.
investigations.hint_1: Use the three hunts above. Do not generalise beyond this lab's profiles.
investigations.hint_2: The labelled vulnerable profile is fail-open on purpose.
investigations.expected_result_shape: No mcp.started after a DENY on the RETEST run.
investigations.result_explanation: A DENY followed by a start would be a control failure; none is expected here.
investigations.security_interpretation: The result is about this lab profile only.
investigations.does_not_prove: Not proof that production MCP authorization is safe.
